vhaccelerator.config.title: VH Accelerator settings
vhaccelerator.config.dialog.default.mess: Every VH Accelerator setting, including Diagnostics, goes back to its shipped default and is saved and applied at once. Unsaved changes on this screen are discarded.
vhaccelerator.config.dialog.experimental:
These settings ship turned off. They will be turned on, saved and applied at once:
%s
Diagnostics are not changed. Unsaved changes on this screen are discarded.
Every experimental setting is already on.
vhaccelerator.config.dialog.restart.mess:
These changes take effect after you restart the game:
%s
vhaccelerator.config.message.cloth_missi: VH Accelerator's settings screen needs Cloth Config. You can still change every setting in config/vhaccelerator-client.toml and config/vhaccelerator-common.toml.
vhaccelerator.config.message.cloth_incom: VH Accelerator's settings screen does not work with this Cloth Config version. You can still change every setting in config/vhaccelerator-client.toml and config/vhaccelerator-common.toml.
vhaccelerator.config.button.report_bug.s: Shows the report first; nothing is uploaded or sent by VH Accelerator.
vhaccelerator.config.button.report_bug.t: Opens a preview of a GitHub issue with your versions, related mods and changed VH Accelerator settings, plus the newest crash report if there is one. Your user folder, name and UUID are removed first. VH Accelerator uploads nothing: it can copy the crash report to your clipboard and open the issue page in your browser, and you submit it yourself.
vhaccelerator.bugreport.title: Report a VH Accelerator bug
vhaccelerator.bugreport.issue_heading: Issue text that opens on GitHub (personal paths and your name are removed):
vhaccelerator.bugreport.crash_heading: Crash report that will be copied to your clipboard (%s):
vhaccelerator.bugreport.status.hint: Nothing is uploaded. Scroll to read everything; you submit the issue yourself on GitHub.
vhaccelerator.config.general.enableClien: Main switch for the client-side speed-ups.

Controls the speed-ups that only run on your own game, not on a server. Turn it off to see how the game behaves without them, or to rule them out when something looks wrong. The speed-ups that work while you play follow the switch right away, but the ones that run during launch only change after a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.overlapModel: Prepares model and block lists at the same time during launch.

While the game reads model files at launch, it also starts preparing its lists of block and model names instead of doing these jobs one after another. Everything finishes before the game goes on. Turn it off only to compare launch times. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.parallelMode: Reads ordinary model files on several threads at launch.

Reads and checks plain model files on several processor threads instead of one. Models that need special loaders, and any that fail, still load the normal way. Turn it off if models look wrong or to compare launch times. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.parallelBloc: Reads block definition files on several threads at launch.

Reads the files that say which model each block uses on several threads at once. The game and Forge still read the contents the usual way, and BuildScape, unknown blocks and any failures use the old path. Turn it off if blocks look wrong. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.parallelAtla: Experimental. Builds texture sheets on several threads at launch.

Experimental. Builds the game's texture sheets at the same time instead of one by one. Some mods react to this step and can break when several run at once, so it is off by default and known to cause problems in some large packs. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.serializeAtl: Keeps mod texture hooks one at a time if sheets build in parallel.

Only matters when "Build texture sheets in parallel" is on. It runs every mod's texture-sheet hook one at a time first and builds the sheets in parallel afterwards, so mods never run at the same time. Leave it on. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.parallelMode: Builds block and item models on background threads at launch.

Prepares the game's models for drawing in batches on background threads instead of one at a time. If a batch fails, the models are redone one by one the safe way. Turn it off if models look wrong or to compare launch times. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.optimizeVoxe: Speeds up building block hit boxes while mods load.

Uses a quicker method to combine the hit-box shapes of complex blocks as they are registered. The result is the same as the normal method, and it helps most in packs with many decoration blocks. It steps aside on its own if Canary or Lithium is installed. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.cacheLaunchV: Shares identical block shapes while mods load.

While mods load, identical block shapes are shared and repeated shape joins are reused instead of being worked out again for every block and wood type. The shared data is freed once loading finishes. It steps aside if Canary or Lithium is installed. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.asyncCrashRe: Moves a small startup chore to a background thread.

At startup Minecraft builds a throwaway crash report just to load its crash-reporting code. This does that on a background thread so loading does not wait for it. Real crash reports are not affected. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.persistentMo: Saves the list of model files so later launches start faster.

Keeps a file on disk with the model files found at launch and reuses it only when your mods, resource packs and relevant settings are unchanged. The game still reads every model itself, and reloading in game with F3+T never uses it. Turn it off if models look out of date after changing packs. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.prewarmPersi: Starts reading saved models before the game needs them.

Works with the saved model list. It starts reading ordinary models early, before the game would otherwise wait for them, and only uses the result when your pack is unchanged since the list was saved. Models with special loaders, BuildScape models and failures load the normal way. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.separateMode: Lets disk reading and model checking overlap during launch.

Frees up the disk-reading step so it can move on while the processor checks the models already read. Everything still finishes before the game goes on. Turn it off to compare with the original combined step. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.optimizeMate: Avoids extra copying when restoring saved texture lists.

When the saved texture lists are loaded at launch, this skips a bulk copy and some repeated name parsing. The same safety checks still run for every list. Only matters if the texture-list cache is on. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.memory.releaseCache: Drops launch cache copies from memory once they are used.

The saved cache files stay on disk and are read again when needed, but the copies held in memory during play are released. Turn it off only if you have plenty of memory and want to keep them. Part of this runs during launch, so it needs a restart to change; the clean-up after JEI starts follows the setting right away.
vhaccelerator.config.memory.releaseBaker: Releases model loading tables once models are applied.

Forge keeps the last model loader alive for the whole session. This releases its large temporary tables after the models are in use, while keeping what is still needed. Turn it off if a mod misbehaves after a reload. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.takeOverBuil: VH Accelerator loads BuildScape's models with the rest.

Only with BuildScape installed. VH Accelerator loads and builds BuildScape's models like any other, and BuildScape skips its own parallel loading. Turn it off to let BuildScape use its own launch speed-ups. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.isolateBackg: Runs optional online checks away from the loading threads.

Some mods check online while loading, and those checks can block. This runs them on their own small set of threads (at most two) so they do not hold up model loading. Connection time limits are unchanged. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.persistentBl: Saves the block definition files so later launches start faster.

Like the saved model list, but for the files that say which model each block uses. The contents are still checked fresh against the current blocks, and it is reused only when your pack is unchanged. Reloading in game with F3+T never uses it. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.preSizeModel: Sizes the model tables up front to avoid repeated resizing.

Sets the size of the game's big model tables from the number of blocks and items, instead of letting them grow step by step. It helps in packs with a very large number of block states. If another mod has replaced one of the tables, that table is left alone. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.stageModelCa: Sets table sizes again once the real model count is known.

Builds on "Reserve model table space". It sizes the baked-model tables when baking starts, using the real count of models found instead of an estimate. Turn it off to compare with the earlier sizing. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.preSizeFerri: Remembers FerriteCore's table size for faster later launches.

Only with FerriteCore installed. FerriteCore uses a very large temporary table while loading, and this learns its size for your pack and pre-sizes it next time (only a number is saved, no model data). Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.promoteCache: Avoids looking up the same loaded model twice at launch.
Minecraft looks up and stores every cached block model a second time for no benefit. This puts an already-loaded model straight into place instead. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.asyncUserApi: Sets up the online account service without holding up startup.

Creates the connection to Minecraft's online account services on a background thread so launch does not wait for it. The finished connection is still used afterwards, behind a wrapper that never blocks. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.memoizeModel: Stops the game working out each model's textures repeatedly.
For each model, the game works out which textures it uses by walking through its parent models. This remembers the answer for each model so the walk is not repeated. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.persistentMo: Saves which textures each model uses for later launches.

Keeps the per-model texture lists on disk and uses them only if your whole pack matches and the models can safely be linked to their parents. Special models, changing models, missing textures and in-game reloads use the normal path. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.deduplicateM: Collects textures once for identical models.

When many block states point at the same model, the textures are collected once instead of once per state. Special and changing models keep the original behavior. It helps most in packs with many look-alike blocks. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.cacheBlockSt: Builds each block state's model name once, not twice.
Minecraft builds the same text name for each block state twice during launch. This keeps the first one and reuses it. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.memory.compactModel: Stores simple model data in exact-size lists.

Stores each simple model's face lists in exact-size lists and shares one empty table. This saves memory without changing how anything looks. It is skipped when Vault Render Optimization is installed, because that does the same. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.lazyBakeEven: Stops some mods forcing every model to be built at launch.

Needs "Delay block models until used". Mods such as Create, Mekanism and Refined Storage only wrap models during loading; this hands them a stand-in that is built when first used, so those mods no longer force the real build at launch. CTM and FramedBlocks still get real models. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.parallelCraf: Finds recipes to remove on several threads.

Only with CraftTweaker installed. Recipe removals by output, input or mod are matched on worker threads, and the recipes are then removed on the calling thread. Removals that use script-written conditions keep the original loop. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.indexCreateB: Speeds up Create's block-cutting page in JEI.

Only with Create 0.5.1.i and JEI. Stonecutting recipes for Create's block-cutting page are grouped by ingredient instead of comparing every recipe with every group. The groups, order and results are the same. Applies from the next JEI start (world join).
vhaccelerator.config.vault.indexVaultSme: Speeds up the Vault tool-smelting page in JEI.
Only with Vault Hunters and JEI. The tool-smelting page used to check every smelting recipe for each of about 39,000 items. This builds one lookup instead, in the same order.
vhaccelerator.config.vault.indexVaultCas: Keeps long cake vaults from slowing down with each cake.

Only for Vault Hunters builds without grouped modifiers (such as 3.21.6 and 20.0.3), and only in singleplayer. Cascade modifiers look up their stack count from an index instead of scanning every modifier for every generated chunk. The result is the same.
vhaccelerator.config.vault.cacheVaultMod: Reuses the vault modifier list instead of rebuilding it.

Only with Vault Hunters. The list of vault modifiers, used by the HUD every frame and by potion and trinket checks every tick, is reused until it changes or a quarter of a second passes. Long cake vaults add many entries, so this matters most there. Callers get copies.
vhaccelerator.config.vault.indexVaultMod: Updates only new or timed modifiers each tick.

Only with Vault Hunters, and only in singleplayer. Each tick Vault Hunters walks every modifier three times; this visits only the new or timed ones. Ticks with anything to apply or expire use Vault's own code. Long cake vaults hold thousands of permanent entries.
vhaccelerator.config.vault.snapshotVault: Stops copying every event listener list on every event.

Only with Vault Hunters. Its own event system now runs listeners from a snapshot taken when listeners change, instead of copying the lists for each event, and spawn and despawn checks send one every tick for every mob. The order is the same. Client drawing events are left to Vault Render Optimization.
vhaccelerator.config.vault.filterVaultCa: Cascade modifiers skip blocks they would ignore anyway.

Only with Vault Hunters, and only in singleplayer. Cascade modifiers skip building the saved data for blocks that already fail their filter, such as the thousands of ores in a late cake vault's mine rooms. The outcome is the same.
vhaccelerator.config.vault.repairEmptyBo: Stops magenta "Missing: book_pile" blocks in library rooms.

Only with Vault Hunters and Supplementaries, and only in singleplayer. Some library room templates store book piles without any books, which then show as magenta error blocks. Such piles now load with as many plain books as the block shows, at least one.
vhaccelerator.config.join.prefetchJoinRe: Begins checking the saved recipe list as soon as you join.

When you join a world, the check that decides whether the saved JEI recipe list can be reused starts in the background right away instead of waiting for JEI. The check itself is the same. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.prefetchCtmT: Reads Connected Textures data on several threads.

Only with CTM 1.1.5+5. Reads each texture's connected-texture data in parallel before CTM asks for it, so CTM finds it ready. Anything that fails is left for CTM to read and report. Applies from the next resource reload (F3+T).
vhaccelerator.config.compat.indexKubeJsP: Answers KubeJS file checks from one listing.

Only with KubeJS 1802.5.5. KubeJS checks the disk for every resource lookup. This lists its asset and data folders once per reload and answers the checks from that list, so turn it off if KubeJS files do not show up after you edit them. Applies from the next resource reload (F3+T).
vhaccelerator.config.compat.lazyGeckoLib: Loads animation and model files when first drawn.

Only with GeckoLib 3.0.57 (and Ars Nouveau 2.9.0's copy). Instead of parsing every animation and model file of every mod during a reload, it loads each one the first time it is drawn. Turn it off if an animated mob looks wrong. Applies from the next resource reload (F3+T).
vhaccelerator.config.compat.persistentEv: Saves Every Compat's generated textures between launches.

Only with Every Compat and Selene 1.17.14 or 1.17.17. The resource pack it generates is saved on disk and restored next launch, as long as mods, blocks, configs and resource packs match. Turn it off if Every Compat blocks look stale. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.join.suspendIntegra: Holds your singleplayer world still until you have fully joined.

In singleplayer, the world waits to run its ticks until your game has processed the join data (recipes, tags, JEI start), for at most 60 seconds. Chunks keep loading meanwhile. It does not affect LAN guests or proxy servers. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.memory.deduplicateM: Keeps one copy of each block or item name in memory.
Large packs create about 1.3 million model names, many with the same text. This shares one copy of each. Only memory changes. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.parallelBloc: Works out block model names on several threads at launch.

Prepares the model names for blocks across all your processor cores before the game needs them. It uses Minecraft's own name builder, so names come out exactly the same, including those from mods. Needs a restart.
Fills the block-to-model table on several threads.

After mods have changed the models, the game builds a table that says which model each block state uses. This builds the table on several threads and only uses it once all are done. If anything fails, the game's normal method runs instead. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.deferItemMod: Builds inventory item models the first time you see them.

Plain item models are built when first drawn instead of all at launch, which shortens loading. Items with special models and Vault gear are still built at launch, and it switches itself off with ModernFix's dynamic resources, in Compare Mode and during in-world reloads. Turn it off if an item looks wrong. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.deferBlockSt: Builds plain block models the first time they are needed.

Plain block models are built when first needed, usually while the world draws a chunk, instead of all at launch. Special and changing models are still built at launch, and it switches itself off with ModernFix's dynamic resources, in Compare Mode and during in-world reloads. Turn it off if a block looks wrong. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.skipBlockSta: Later launches skip re-reading plain block files.

Needs "Delay block models until used". The first launch checks which blocks are plain, and later launches with the same assets skip reading those blocks' files and load them when first needed (blocks with CTM textures are never skipped). Turn it off if blocks look wrong after a pack change. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.diagnostics.recordB: Experimental. Saves research data only. No speed or memory gain.

Experimental. On the first launch it writes a list of block textures and model groups to a file in the cache folder, for later experiments. Nothing reads that file yet, so it does not speed up launches or save memory, and it adds a small cost to that launch. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.protectDynam: Keeps special or changing models on the safe one-thread path.

Models from mods that change or build themselves while the game runs stay on Minecraft's normal single-thread loading. If a parallel build fails, every model is redone one by one. Leave this on unless you are testing this safety check itself. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.indexModelBa: Speeds up how mods look up models during launch.

Some mods search the whole list of baked models during launch. This sorts the list by mod once so they can find theirs quickly. The order of mod hooks and the changes they make are unchanged. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.memoizeCtmMo: Reuses CTM's model results while models are built.
Only with the tested CTM 1.18.2 build. When several blocks share a model, CTM's result is reused during one model-build step; CTM still handles every matching model. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.disableEvery: Stops Every Compat writing a big debug copy each launch.

Only with the tested Every Compat and Selene 1.18.2 builds. Every Compat writes a large copy of its generated resources to a debug folder on each launch; this skips it. The game's own textures are generated as normal. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.cacheDecocra: Parses each Decocraft model file once, not per variant.

Only with the tested Decocraft build. Many material variants point to the same Blockbench model file; this reads it once and reuses it. The saved copy lives in memory only and is cleared on every reload. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.join.parallelJeiIng: Sorts JEI's item list on several threads when you join.

Only with JEI installed. JEI sorts its item list with a dedicated group of worker threads, which it scales back once you are playing. JEI is not shown as ready until the sort is finished. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.indexPowahWi: Indexes recipes once for Powah's in-game wiki.

Only with Powah installed. The in-game wiki used to scan the whole recipe list repeatedly after each server connection. It now builds one index of crafting and smelting recipes. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.parallelJeiT: Matches JEITweaker hidden items on several threads.

Only with JEI and JEITweaker installed. Hidden ingredients are matched in parallel against a fixed snapshot. Removals while playing stay in order, and any failure goes back to the original method. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.jeiTweakerPa: Smallest item count that uses the parallel JEITweaker match.

Only used when "Faster JEITweaker hiding" is on. Hidden-item matching only switches to several threads when JEI has at least this many ingredients; below it, the single-thread method is used. The default is fine for nearly everyone. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.vault.stagedVaultGr: Builds Vault block and mob groups in small slices.

Only with Vault Hunters. Instead of one long pause, the groups are built a little each tick and only used once complete. Nothing outside the main game thread touches live mobs. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.vault.optimizeVault: Speeds up how Vault Hunters builds its loot odds.

Only with Vault Hunters. When Vault Hunters works out the odds for its tiered loot it uses a faster method that gives the same odds in the same order. Takes effect the next time Vault Hunters builds its loot settings; restart to be sure.
vhaccelerator.config.vault.lazyVaultLoot: Work out loot odds on demand
Builds each loot table's odds only when first needed.

Only with Vault Hunters. Vault Hunters builds 53 sets of odds for every supported loot table, which takes memory and time, and a multiplayer client never uses them. This builds each one the first time loot needs it. Takes effect the next time Vault Hunters loads its settings; restart to be sure.
vhaccelerator.config.vault.vaultGroupTic: Most time spent per tick on spread-out vault group setup.

Only used when "Spread out vault group setup" is on. A higher number finishes the setup sooner but can cause a short stutter; a lower number is smoother but takes longer. The unit is milliseconds per game tick.
vhaccelerator.config.join.asyncJeiSearch: Builds JEI's search list on a worker thread.
Only with JEI installed. JEI's search list is built on a separate worker and swapped in when complete. If the worker fails, the main thread builds it the normal way. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.join.parallelJeiSea: Fills JEI's search tables on several threads.

Only with JEI installed. JEI keeps several separate search tables, and this fills them at the same time. The finished set is only used once all are done, and any failure uses the one-at-a-time method. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.join.optimizeJeiIng: Skips repeated bookkeeping while JEI builds its item filter.

Only with JEI installed. JEI repeats some identity and cache work while it builds its first item filter. This avoids that for ordinary items, but only if JEI's hidden-item lists are empty; otherwise JEI's own checks run. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.join.persistentVani: Saves JEI's list of vanilla items between launches.

Only with JEI installed. The finished item list is saved on disk and reused only if the server, mods, item registry, tags and configs all match. If anything differs, JEI builds the list normally. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.join.parallelVanill: Checks JEI's vanilla recipe lists on several threads.

Only with JEI installed. The crafting, furnace, smithing and similar recipe lists are checked by a small pool of workers, with the order kept. If anything fails, JEI's normal one-at-a-time check runs. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.join.persistentVani: Saves which JEI recipes passed the check. Often not faster.

Only with JEI installed. Saves the IDs of recipes that passed JEI's check and reuses them when mods, tags and configs match. It is off by default because loading a long saved list can cost more time than the parallel check it replaces. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.join.persistentJeiR: Saves JEI's recipe-to-ingredient index between launches.

Only with JEI installed. Saves the index that links recipes to their ingredients and reuses it only when recipes, tags, configs, mods, server and JEI match. A mismatch rebuilds it normally. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.cacheJerComp: Loads JER loot data in the menus and reuses it.

Only with Just Enough Resources installed. Its loot tables are loaded in the background while you are in the menus, and the result is reused when JEI is rebuilt. If you connect before it finishes, the game waits for the rest. Applies from the next time the main menu opens or you join a world.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.parallelCraf: Decodes CraftTweaker's synced tags on several threads.

Only with CraftTweaker installed. Each tag set is built in its own memory and only used once all are done. If anything fails, CraftTweaker's own method is used instead. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.compactCraft: Shrinks repeated CraftTweaker messages in the log.

Only with CraftTweaker installed, when your game replays the server's scripts and would normally log one line per action. This combines those lines and keeps warnings, errors and script names. Turn it off if you need every action in crafttweaker.log. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.parallelTher: Refreshes Thermal's machine recipes on several threads.

Only with Thermal installed. Independent recipe lists are refreshed together, a duplicate fuel scan is postponed and the saved fuel values are restored when tags and configs match. The game still waits until every list is finished before you see the world. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.cacheIronFur: Builds Iron Furnaces' fuel and smoking lists once per session.

Only with Iron Furnaces and JEI. The fuel and smoking recipe lists are built in one pass and reused for later JEI rebuilds in the same game session. Generator recipes tied to the world are always read fresh. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.persistentIr: Saves Iron Furnaces fuel results between launches.

Only with Iron Furnaces installed. The checked fuel list is saved and reused only if tags, configs, mod files and the item registry match. If it does not match, the list is rebuilt before you see the world. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.precompileIr: Builds Iron Furnaces' smoking list during the main menu.

Only with Iron Furnaces installed. The smoking list, which does not depend on the server, is built in small slices while you sit in the menus. Fuel times are always worked out once you are in a world, so server settings apply. Applies from the next time the main menu opens.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.ironFurnaces: Most time the menu spends on the Iron Furnaces pre-build.
Only used when "Pre-build Iron Furnaces list" is on. A higher number finishes sooner but can make the menu stutter; a lower number keeps the menu smooth. The unit is milliseconds per frame.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.optimizeIndu: Builds Industrial Foregoing stonework recipes more quickly.

Only with Industrial Foregoing and JEI. Stonework combinations are built step by step, and JEI is given only the shortest way to each output. Results still come from the server's recipes. Applies from the next world join.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.deferXaeroOn: Runs Xaero's update and Patreon checks after the menu appears.
Only with the tested versions of Xaero's Minimap and World Map. Their online checks no longer hold up loading; they start on one low-priority thread after the first menu frame. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.boundFarsigh: Drops far chunks the server unloaded that Farsight keeps.

Only with Farsight installed, and not when Vault Render Optimization is also there (it handles this itself). Chunks the server has unloaded are forgotten once they are beyond the view distance plus one, checked once a second. Chunks within your render distance stay. Turn it off if far terrain disappears.
vhaccelerator.config.vault.deferVaultAtl: Uploads Vault's menu textures during the loading screen fade.

Only with Vault Hunters. The initial upload of Vault's menu texture sheets is moved out of the loading wait and done one sheet per frame during the loading screen's two-second fade. The loading screen stays until every sheet is ready, and reloading in game (F3+T) uses the normal method. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.vault.cacheVaultToo: Remembers Vault item tooltip lookups so hovering is quicker.

Only with Vault Hunters, and only while client optimizations are on. Remembers tooltip lookups by item and language so they are not repeated each time you hover. Turn it off if tooltips look stale after changing language or packs.
vhaccelerator.config.vault.optimizeVault: Skips a warning-only texture check unless debug is on.

Only with Vault Hunters. Vault's check for missing or unused textures only writes warnings, so it is skipped unless the debug setting is on, and then it counts the same entries faster. Textures themselves are never changed. Applies from the next resource reload (F3+T).
vhaccelerator.config.diagnostics.profile: Times loading phases. Does nothing unless Debug logging is on.

Measures each phase of game loading and logs any resource step that takes 20 milliseconds or longer. It only runs while "Debug logging" is also on, so with default settings it does nothing. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.general.checkForUpd: Looks online for new VH Accelerator versions and tells you.
Checks the mod's GitHub page in the background. When a newer version exists it shows a notice on the main menu and now and then in chat. Turn it off if you do not want the mod to contact GitHub.
vhaccelerator.config.general.updateTypes: Choose between critical updates only or every update.
Critical shows only updates the author has marked as critical. All also shows normal updates. This only matters while update checks are on.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.deferTargetD: Fixes a startup crash risk in Target Dummy 1.5.2.

Only with Target Dummy 1.18-1.5.2. That version writes to a shared list while mods load in parallel; this makes only its dispenser step run in the safe place. It is a fix, not a speed-up, and other versions are untouched. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.memory.trimDecocraf: Cuts the memory Decocraft's models use.

Only with Decocraft 3.0.4. Block variants of the same model share one copy, and image data and file paths that Decocraft never uses again are cleared. In big packs this can free a large amount of memory, and models, textures and hit boxes are unchanged. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.memory.compactFerri: Saves memory per block state when FerriteCore is present.

Only with FerriteCore 4.2.2. Drops a small helper object that FerriteCore keeps for every block and fluid state, which adds up in packs with over a million states. Property lookups use FerriteCore's shared data directly. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.memory.releaseLevel: Stops leftovers from holding a world in memory after you leave.

Clears things that keep a whole world in memory after you leave it: an item entity on the shared empty item, Forge's model-data caches, and Copycats+'s link to the singleplayer server. A restart is needed for it to be fully on or off. Part of the clean-up reads the setting every time a singleplayer world stops.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.restoreSmoot: Keeps Smooth Boot from starving loading work.

Only with Smooth Boot (Reloaded) installed. Smooth Boot lowers the priority of several loading threads, which can starve VH Accelerator's parallel work when the processor is busy. This raises them back to normal and never lowers any, and Compare Mode turns it off. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.diagnostics.compare: Turns off all VH Accelerator speed-ups for a fair comparison.

Disables every VH Accelerator optimization so you can measure the game without it. Timers and debug output still work if enabled. Saving this setting takes effect for the running game at once, but restart before comparing launch times, because some changes are only chosen at startup.
Shows login and server-switch timings in chat and the log.
Shows how long logging in, switching servers and disconnecting take, in chat, and writes summaries to the log. The launch-time line on the main menu stays visible either way. Safe to leave off.
vhaccelerator.config.diagnostics.debug.s: Writes detailed loading and connection diagnostics to the log.
vhaccelerator.config.diagnostics.debug.t: Records detailed information about launch, reloads, models and connections. It adds measuring and logging work, so leave it off for normal play. Needs a restart, because the diagnostic parts are chosen at startup.
vhaccelerator.config.diagnostics.jeiReci: Logs recipe IDs when the saved JEI index repairs a recipe.

Only with JEI installed. When VH Accelerator's saved JEI index has to repair a recipe at login, the exact recipe ID and what differed are written to the log. For troubleshooting only, and it works without turning on debug logging.
vhaccelerator.config.general.enableCommo: Main switch for speed-ups shared by singleplayer and servers.

Controls the speed-ups that work the same on your own game and on a dedicated server, such as faster resource reloads and chunk reading. Turn it off to rule them out when something looks wrong. Part of it is applied while the game starts, so changing it only takes full effect after a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.server.streamlineOb: Tidies up after mod loading a little faster.

Refines a clean-up step run once after mods have loaded, with early safety exits and one check per registry. It needs the "Redundant object-holder cleanup" backport to be on. Turn it off to use the original per-item checks. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.server.parallelRelo: Adds measuring to resource reloads. No speed-up today.

Minecraft 1.18.2 already prepares reload steps side by side, so this does not currently make reloads faster. It adds timing and a place for future reload improvements, which is why it is off by default. Applies from the next resource or data reload.
vhaccelerator.config.server.skipRedundan: Experimental. Skips some startup checks and may miss problems.

Experimental. Skips two out of three of the game's registry checks while loading, which can let a problem in an unrelated registry go unnoticed. It is off until measurements show it is worth it, so leave it off unless you know why you want it. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.server.skipRegistry: Skips Forge's registry dump, which normally does nothing.
Forge only builds its registry dump tables when a certain debug log level is on, so this normally changes nothing. Turn it on only if you are sure you never need that debug output. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.server.parallelBloc: Experimental. Prepares block state data on several threads.

Experimental. Prepares the block state caches on several threads while the block list is being finished. It is ignored when "Lazy block data" is on and turned off when ModernFix is present. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.server.lazyBlockSta: Experimental. Delays block data setup and may break modded blocks.

Experimental. Holds back building each block's cached data until something asks for it. Modded blocks may read parts that are not ready, so it is off by default and should be turned off if blocks act oddly. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.launch.cacheResourc: Reuses repeated resource searches until the next reload.

The game often asks for the same list of resource files many times. This keeps the answer until the next reload. Turn it off if a resource pack change does not show up. Applies from the next resource reload (F3+T).
vhaccelerator.config.server.indexImmutab: Keeps a quick index of the files inside mod jars.

Builds an index of the files inside each mod jar as needed, so repeated searches for models, block files, textures and "does this exist" checks are quick. Folder packs, packs generated while running, and suspicious scans use the normal path. This one setting is also the "Immutable resource-pack tree indexing" backport, so it is only listed here. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.compat.parallelKube: Matches KubeJS recipe filters on several threads.

Only with KubeJS 1802.5.5-build.569. Recipe remove and forEachRecipe filters that use only KubeJS's built-in filters are matched in parallel, then applied in the original order. Script functions and custom conditions stay on one thread. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.server.asyncChunkDi: Read chunks off the main thread
Reads world chunks from disk without stalling the game.

The disk read and unpacking of each loaded chunk now happens on the chunk IO thread instead of blocking the main server thread (vanilla did the same in 1.19). The rest still runs on the main thread in the usual order. Works in singleplayer and on dedicated servers. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.server.skipReturnin: Skips a world-spawn search whose result is thrown away.

When you log in with saved player data, or respawn at a valid bed or anchor, the game searches around the world spawn and then ignores the result. This skips that search. New players and players without a respawn point still get the normal search. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.forgeHand: Speeds up the mod list exchange when you join a server.
Lets the Forge join handshake process several packets in a row instead of waiting between each one. Helps joining servers with large mod lists. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.attribute: Uses less memory by sharing identical mob attribute data.
Mobs with identical attribute settings share one copy of the data instead of each keeping its own. Only memory use changes. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.attachCap: Speeds up how Forge hands out capabilities to objects.
Speeds up the Forge step that lets mods attach extra data to entities, items and blocks as they are created. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.compactMo: Uses less memory for the scan data Forge keeps about mods.
Forge keeps records of what it found in every mod file. This stores them in a smaller form with shared values. Only memory use changes. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.forgeTagC: Fixes rare crashes when mods load tags at the same time.
Makes Forge's tag lists safe when several threads use them at once. It is a stability fix. Turn it off only when testing. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.serverEve: Stops the server main thread wasting time while it waits.
Corrects how the server waits between ticks, so it does not spin and burn processor time when it has nothing to do. Applies to singleplayer worlds and servers. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.overrideM: Use VHA instead of MF dynamic
Client only. Replaces ModernFix's dynamic resources with VHA's.

Client only; does nothing on a server. Only with ModernFix installed. VH Accelerator's own model loading is used instead of ModernFix's dynamic resources feature, which stays off; turn it off to let ModernFix keep that job. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.responsiv: Client only. Stops small waits while mods load.

Client only; does nothing on a server. During mod loading the main thread used to notice finished steps up to tens of milliseconds late, many times per launch. This makes it respond sooner. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.modernFix: Client only. Fixes false "server not responding" shutdowns.

Client only; does nothing on a server. Only with ModernFix installed. Corrects the timing of the singleplayer watchdog that watches for a stuck world, especially while the world is still starting. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.stateDefi: Makes block state setup more forgiving and faster.
Builds the table of a block's state combinations in a way that falls back to a complete safe table if needed. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.compactPa: Guards a memory-saving block storage trick against bad data.
Chunks store blocks in compact lists. This adds a guard so a broken list is handled safely instead of crashing. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.modernFix: Client only. Stops a JEI search glitch with ModernFix.
Client only; does nothing on a server. Only with ModernFix and JEI installed. Takes a snapshot of JEI's search results before reading them, so the list cannot change mid-search. Needs a restart.
Keeps ModernFix's config-reload delay from misbehaving.
Only with ModernFix installed. Corrects ModernFix's one-second delay on reacting to config file changes. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.backgroun: Client only. Caps how many background threads Minecraft makes.

Client only; does nothing on a server. Sets a sensible limit on Minecraft's background threads for your processor, unless you already set one yourself. Fewer threads can leave more room for the game. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.compactEn: Client only. Uses less memory for mob and entity models.
Client only; does nothing on a server. Entity model parts that are the same share one copy. Only memory use changes. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.worldgenM: Speeds up terrain generation with fewer short-lived objects.
Walks through terrain material rules without creating extra temporary objects. Affects new terrain generation. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.worldgenS: Speeds up surface layer generation in new terrain.
Walks through the rules that decide surface blocks without creating extra temporary objects. Affects new terrain generation. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.worldgenN: Speeds up a lookup used when generating terrain.
Speeds up how terrain generation finds its noise functions. Affects new terrain generation. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.worldgenB: Avoids repeating biome lookups during terrain generation.
Reuses a biome lookup during surface generation instead of recomputing it for the same position. Affects new terrain generation. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.worldgenD: Speeds up height checks used in terrain generation.
Evaluates height conditions in surface rules directly. Affects new terrain generation. Needs a restart.
Builds biome climate data only when first needed.
Waits to build the biome climate lookup until the world needs it, which can shorten the wait for a world to start. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.earlyStru: When the game looks for where a structure can go, it now throws out impossible spots sooner. Affects new terrain and structure searches. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.compactOb: Releases leftover debugging data from mod loading.
After a successful load, Forge's registry callbacks keep error traces that are never needed again. This frees them, saving a little memory. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.removeRed: Removes unneeded Forge callbacks after mods load.
Removes registry callbacks that do nothing after loading, to save memory and time. "Streamlined holder cleanup" in the Server & engine tab builds on this. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.fasterLoo: Speeds up reading loot tables on load or reload.
Reuses the knowledge of which mod each loot table file comes from instead of working it out repeatedly. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.dynamicCl: Client only. Stores text translations in less memory.
Client only; does nothing on a server. Reads language files once and stores the text compactly, which saves memory in big packs. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.disableTe: Client only. Stops Minecraft sending usage telemetry.
Client only; does nothing on a server. Blocks the usage data Minecraft would send to Mojang, while all other online services work as before. Turn it off if you want telemetry sent. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.fasterIng: Speeds up recipe ingredient tag checks.
Speeds up how recipe ingredients that use item tags are looked up. Helps with large recipe lists. Needs a restart.
Keeps expanded ingredient lists around, but can free them.
Remembers each recipe ingredient's expanded item list instead of rebuilding it, and lets the game free the copy if memory gets tight. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.ingredien: Uses less memory by sharing identical ingredient data.
Identical recipe ingredient entries share one copy. Only memory use changes. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.mappedReg: Speeds up registering many blocks and items.
Grows Minecraft's registry tables in larger steps, so they are resized fewer times when many entries are added. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.forgeRegi: Cuts temporary objects created by Forge registry lookups.
Removes small temporary objects created each time Forge looks up a registered item or block. Needs a restart.
Speeds up Forge registering items and blocks at startup.
Speeds up checks Forge does while mods register blocks, items and other entries. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.deduplica: Keeps one copy of each mod ID text in memory.
Every named game object stores its mod ID as text, with many repeated copies. This shares one copy per mod. Only memory use changes. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.blockProp: Keeps one copy of each block property name.
Block properties like "facing" repeat across thousands of blocks. This shares one copy of each name. Only memory use changes. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.deduplica: Uses less memory for wall block shape data.
Wall blocks from different mods that need the same shapes share them. Only memory use changes. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.potential: Cuts copying of mob spawn lists while the world runs.
Stops Forge from copying its list of possible mob spawns over and over, copying only when a mod changes it. Helps the world tick with fewer temporary objects. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.reduceTic: Cuts temporary objects made while chunks tick.
Reduces the small temporary objects created each tick for loaded chunks and a few mobs such as bats. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.resourceK: Reuses resource key objects instead of creating new copies each time. Only memory and speed change. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.fasterIng: Checks whether an ingredient is empty without extra work.
Checks whether a recipe ingredient is empty without building temporary lists. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.debugLeve: Avoids an extra copy when making a debug world.
The debug world type makes its own copy of the list of every block state. This reads the existing list instead. It only affects debug worlds. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.fastRegis: Speeds up Forge's final registry check at startup.
Checks Forge's registries when loading finishes without building lists of temporary objects. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.config.backports.stronghol: When the game works out where strongholds go, it throws out impossible positions sooner. Affects new terrain and stronghold searches. Needs a restart.
vhaccelerator.jei.reload.start: [VH Accelerator] Rebuilding JEI from the live recipe and tag state. The game may pause briefly.
vhaccelerator.jei.reload.done: [VH Accelerator] JEI rebuilt from live data in %ss. VHA's JEI caches and parallel index paths were bypassed for this reload.
